study.question: Can information-equivalent constant scaling of the r0052 real-click match-action contrast explain the routing-dependent loss from removing its adaptive radius?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation, all same frozen single seed: g1-r0051-match_nomean_click_shared AUC 0.6647595313 versus g1-r0052-match_unit_click_shared 0.6635006432 (unit minus adaptive = -0.0012588881); task counterparts 0.6659594521 versus 0.6660232354 (+0.0000637833). Shifted shared changed 0.6619936316 to 0.6618874428 (-0.0001061888). Thus the shared adaptive-to-unit penalty is much larger with true placement, but radius information, input scale, rounding and optimization are confounded. The r0052 real-versus-shift gaps are 0.0022898415 task and 0.0016132004 shared. These are observations, not repeated mechanism evidence. Review of trajectories: r0024 zero/context replacements were poor (0.6411900073/0.6414296870), r0034 item-duplicate replacement 0.6637250089 failed to preserve observed-action quality, r0037 stopped observed still beat stopped duplicate (0.6661693800 versus 0.6636235974), r0045 residual projection reversed the preferred real/shift pattern (0.6642468841 versus 0.6660166195), and r0049 opposite-partition radius was unsuccessful for real/shared (0.6623665076). These negative branches rule out a simple any-representation-is-equivalent story but do not refute historical feedback utility. No failure status is exposed in the current trajectory index and previous_runtime_error is null; omitted older branches are not presumed successful. The incumbent remains 0.6667535475, above every proposed parent; DIN is 0.6555440824. No new outcome is available. Mechanism hypothesis: the scale of the two synthetic match-action inputs changes their balance with item/ordinal inputs in the residual ReLU banks and their optimization under the fixed recipe. A shared readout may be more sensitive to that balance than task routing. If so, at least one of two reciprocal fixed scales may recover a material fraction of the shared unit-radius penalty without reintroducing action-vector radius information. This is a calibration/optimization attribution hypothesis, not a claimed novel predictive mechanism. A null result only constrains the tested amplitudes.

No priority or exact-paper-reproduction claim.

All embedding, target/context/item fields, uniform compressed DIN click route, auxiliary feedback route, source ownership, Dice support and unnormalized pooling.

study.proposed_difference: Add architecture-only summary_radius_scale with admitted values 0.25, 1.0, 4.0, restricted to the unit radius source. Set radius32 to its inherited ones_like then multiply by scale when scale !=1, before the canonical zero-mean stream. Four cells cross R=0.25 or4 with task/shared residual routing, all using true click membership. R=1 takes the exact inherited arithmetic and provides a host parity bridge. The two powers of two are predeclared without empirical calibration and preserve the binary significand when representable; subsequent BF16 reductions/activations can still differ. No new information, learned parameter, state, random draw or loss term. These cells study scale/routing, not a new scale-by-placement interaction; unit/shift references remain context and will not be substituted for missing shifted-scale controls.
predictions: If scale/optimization accounts for much of the shared penalty, at least one fixed radius will recover >=0.0006294441 click AUC versus g1-r0052-match_unit_click_shared, half its 0.0012588881 gap to g1-r0051-match_nomean_click_shared. Treat this predeclared effect-size target as descriptive, not a significance threshold.

For each R, report D(R)=[AUC(R,shared)-AUC(1,shared)]-[AUC(R,task)-AUC(1,task)] and all component scores. A routing-dependent scale response, especially shared recovery with a small task change, is provisional support for the stated sensitivity hypothesis. Do not report only the best scale.

At common weights the helper stream scales by R; action-only match rows0/4 scale within declared BF16 tolerance. Item summary coordinates, observed pool, ordinal summary inputs, match counts and masks remain the same. Empty/single-group valid synthetic outputs stay zero. Four-task predictions are initially unchanged because the final adapter layers are zero; after training, downstream predictions need not scale linearly.

Parameter count should remain 32129765 (31793216 embedding,336549 dense) in all cells. Measured training/inference cost should be close to r0052; no efficiency gain is claimed. Report all four AUC/Logloss, utility controls and measured resource/latency values.
falsifiers: No fixed scale recovers the prespecified shared loss fraction: no support for that recovery hypothesis at R=0.25 or4; do not extrapolate to every constant or conclude adaptive information is necessary.

If scale effects in shared and task routing are comparable, the routing-specific account is weakened even if one amplitude improves quality. Worse results at both scales count as negative findings, not a reason to hide a cell or expand the search retrospectively.

Any change to item/ordinal/pool inputs, task masks, gradients into stopped action embeddings, parameter construction or R=1 source parity invalidates the intended isolation; repair before using outcomes for attribution.
Failure to reproduce the response in an authorized paired-seed follow-up weakens the mechanism interpretation. A single seed or a winning variant alone cannot establish the mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Adaptive radii may contain useful historical action-vector information that no constant scale can recover; scaling cannot distinguish all forms of that information.

ReLU thresholds, AdamW coordinate scaling and weight decay, downstream Dice moments, BF16 accumulation and the fixed one-pass optimization trajectory can explain a response without a change in information content.

Task/shared routing has equal instantiated parameter counts but different parameter use, gradient mixing and effective task capacity. A scale-by-routing interaction is not proof of task conditioning independent of those differences.

Observed action pools, ordinal summaries and supplied historical feedback masks remain in the full model. Synthetic match rows alone are independent of learned action vectors; the full model is not action-free. Nonzero R scales are information-equivalent in exact arithmetic, not guaranteed bitwise invertible after rounding.

Validation adaptation across many prior branches, one-seed variation, no paired user-cluster intervals, no raw-data audit in this coding phase and unavailable host tensor diagnostics limit conclusions. Auxiliary task quality is often much worse than DIN; click gains must not conceal those losses. official_offline visibility does not establish point-in-time production validity.
